summary: John's 3rd-great-grandmother; a divorced working nurse of Plymouth who won her divorce and took back her maiden name - praised in 1893 as bearing 'a name beyond reproach'.
bio: Catherine Scott was born at Kingston on 14 May 1837 (Bradsby), 'the third' of six living children of Stephen and Julia Ann Scott; FamilySearch (LHCS-RCM) gives 2 May 1838 and the tree 1836/1837. She was 14 in the 1850 Kingston census (3 Aug 1850). She married Andrew Pringle in 1857 and had seven children. She later sued for divorce - 'the action commenced by her and sustained by the court' - and resumed her maiden name, though she was 'better known by the name of Pringle than Scott'. By 1893 she was a working nurse in Plymouth, a member of the Christian Church, owned a house and lot, had raised her children, and Bradsby wrote that she 'has always had, and now bears, a name beyond reproach... carries on her business with marked ability'. He listed five living children: John (m. Regina Stires), Ellen (m. Francis Randell), Samuel, Orange and Estella - omitting Addison. In 1910 she lived with her son Orange at Larksville. FamilySearch gives her death as 3 Sep 1918 at Larksville, buried 6 Sep 1918 in the Dallas area; the tree shows 1910 as her death year (conflict; 1918 preferred, as she is in the 1910 census).
funFacts: A divorced woman who reverted to her maiden name in the 19th century - rare at the time.
Bradsby's sketch is the only published biography of a direct Pringle-line woman.
